Name the type of every function and procedure when you define it:
the set it takes its argument from (its domain),
the set its values lie in (its codomain),
and, for each input or output, what kind of mathematical object it is.
Say "function", not "rule" or "map",
and link the formal definition of a function at first use.

A procedure that takes several inputs is a function of all of them,
so list each input with its type.
When an output is itself a function,
say so and give its domain and codomain too.

::: {#exm-function-types}

## Typing a procedure's inputs and output

> ❌ A fitting procedure is a rule that takes data
> and produces a prediction.
>
> ✅ A fitting procedure is a function
> from data sets to fitted models.
> A fitted model is a function
> from covariate values to predicted outcomes.

The ❌ version leaves four types unsaid.
"Rule" does not say it is a function.
"Data" does not say it is a data set.
"A prediction" is a single predicted outcome,
but the procedure's output is the fitted model,
which makes a prediction only when given a covariate value.
The ✅ version states each type,
so a reader can check that the output of one
is an acceptable input to the next.

:::

Check each use against the stated types:
a function applied to something outside its domain,
or a value described with the wrong type,
is an error even when the notation looks right.
